name: eventstudies (NIPFP)
what_it_holds: R package (485 commits, CRAN v1.2.2, GPL-2) for event-study methodology from India's National Institute of Public Finance and Policy. Ships sample datasets (SplitDates, StockPriceReturns, OtherReturns) plus an `eventstudy()` function supporting market-model adjustment, custom event windows, cumulative-sum remapping, and bootstrap inference.
why_useful: A mature, peer-reviewed-adjacent event-study toolkit with bootstrap inference (more rigorous than naive t-tests) -- usable for ABNB earnings-day and regulatory-event studies (gap #12 regulatory events, #17 methods).
themes: Event-study and factor packages; earnings-surprise datasets; post-earnings-drift replication; Ken French factor loaders
why_all: A mature, peer-reviewed-adjacent event-study toolkit with bootstrap inference (more rigorous than naive t-tests) -- usable for ABNB earnings-day and regulatory-event studies (gap #12 regulatory events, #17 methods).

name: awesome-prediction-market-apis
what_it_holds: Curated directory of prediction-market APIs, SDKs, MCP servers, and pointers to historical order-book data sources across Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold, Limitless and others; itself an awesome-list (markdown), not a dataset.
why_useful: Fastest way to find which of the many prediction-market API wrappers actually expose historical order-book/price series usable for point-in-time event-probability construction (gap 4, 11, 12) without re-discovering them one by one.
themes: Prediction markets and betting data: Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold APIs and datasets on earnings and travel/regulation events
why_all: Fastest way to find which of the many prediction-market API wrappers actually expose historical order-book/price series usable for point-in-time event-probability construction (gap 4, 11, 12) without re-discovering them one by one.

name: PyManifold
what_it_holds: Python client for the Manifold Markets public API (18 stars, actively maintained through Jan 2026); wraps market listing, bet history, and price/probability history endpoints — Manifold's API is free/keyless for reads.
why_useful: Manifold hosts many community-made questions on company earnings beats, travel/tourism events, and regulatory outcomes; this client is a one-command way to pull full probability history (with timestamps) for any such market — directly serves the point-in-time vintage gap (4) for event-probability nowcasts around the Nov 5 print or regulatory votes (gap 12).
size_hint: small client library, no bundled data
time_coverage: pulls live/historical via API, Manifold history back to 2022
themes: Prediction markets and betting data: Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold APIs and datasets on earnings and travel/regulation events
why_all: Manifold hosts many community-made questions on company earnings beats, travel/tourism events, and regulatory outcomes; this client is a one-command way to pull full probability history (with timestamps) for any such market — directly serves the point-in-time vintage gap (4) for event-probability nowcasts around the Nov 5 print or regulatory votes (gap 12).

name: prediction_markets (futuur)
what_it_holds: Python toolkit unifying Futuur, Manifold Markets, and Polymarket APIs for searching, correlating, and trading; includes market-matching logic across the three platforms by title similarity.
why_useful: Cross-platform market matching would let us assemble a merged event-probability panel (earnings, travel, regulation questions) across three sources rather than one, improving coverage for point-in-time series (gap 4).
themes: Prediction markets and betting data: Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold APIs and datasets on earnings and travel/regulation events
why_all: Cross-platform market matching would let us assemble a merged event-probability panel (earnings, travel, regulation questions) across three sources rather than one, improving coverage for point-in-time series (gap 4).

name: polyledger
what_it_holds: Self-hosted Polymarket indexer that streams on-chain OrderFilled events from Polygon via Envio HyperSync plus CLOB API market metadata into a single queryable DuckDB file ('one file on disk', SQL-queryable). No committed/downloadable dataset — user must run the backfill themselves (a few hours to a couple of days on free tier). MIT licensed, 22 commits, example output timestamped 2026-09-02 suggesting active/recent.
why_useful: A one-command / scriptable method to build a full point-in-time Polymarket trade ledger (all categories) in a DuckDB file the team already uses elsewhere in its stack — lower effort than writing a custom indexer if the team wants an on-chain-verified, timestamped record of Polymarket odds around ABNB earnings or travel/regulation events.
time_coverage: Full Polymarket on-chain history back to inception once backfilled
size_hint: Not stated; scales with full Polymarket trade history
themes: Prediction markets and betting data: Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold APIs and datasets on earnings and travel/regulation events
why_all: A one-command / scriptable method to build a full point-in-time Polymarket trade ledger (all categories) in a DuckDB file the team already uses elsewhere in its stack — lower effort than writing a custom indexer if the team wants an on-chain-verified, timestamped record of Polymarket odds around ABNB earnings or travel/regulation events.
